manifest.hypothesis: POST score (51 req/run, avg 3115 ms) and POST players/add (8 req, avg 4563 ms) are the top two app costs after 004; each CSV row and each player does REPLACE INTO id_generator on MySQL (autocommit, one row lock shared by every concurrent writer) before anything is written, and the upload holds the tenant writer lock meanwhile. Dispensing ids from an in-process counter (hex, seeded from the clock so it never collides with the initial data's ids or with ids from before a restart) removes N MySQL round trips per request.

observations.summary: observe-after-004 (one run): score upload 51x avg 3115ms max 15298ms; players/add 8x avg 4563ms; ranking 1687x avg 24ms; player 1163x avg 5ms; MySQL digest blind (prepared statements); dispenseID in go/isuports.go.

allowedChanges.reason: dispenseID returns fmt.Sprintf("%x", atomic counter seeded from UnixMicro); sync/atomic import

manifest.changeSummary: dispenseID no longer touches MySQL: a process-wide atomic counter seeded from the microsecond clock, formatted as hex like the old ids. id_generator stays in the schema and initialize untouched.
manifest.expectedEffect: Upload and players/add drop from seconds to the SQLite write cost (tens to hundreds of ms); organizer scenarios iterate more; score up beyond the +4% band (plan item 4). Risk: id format accepted by the benchmarker (hex, longer than before: 13 digits).
